newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids steady to up despite softer crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids steady to up despite softer crude.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices were steady to up again Monday despite softer crude, helped by prospects this week for colder East Coast weather though many were out for the Veterans Day holiday or the API conference.

"It's a holiday and there's an API convention, so not much is going on, but we've got a little cold weather and no one wants to sell much," said one cash trader, adding the bias seemed higher with gas more costly and winter approaching.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent buyers raised their sights by a quarter to $19.50 a barrel, with November one percent paper steady to down slightly at $20.00-25.
NYH December one percent paper also was unchanged to softer at $20.75-21.00, while January paper firmed slightly to $21.20-50, traders said.
High sulphurs in NYH were again helped by firmer bunkers, with 2.2 percent gaining slightly to $18.75-19.00.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices were stable, with one percent still at $17.75-$18.00 and three percent at $16.50-75.
USG December three percent paper gained 25-50 cents to the mid-$17 area, traders said.

New York City gate gas prices firmed another 15-20 cents to about the $3.30/mmBtu area on colder weather there. NYH one percent resid was at a $3.12/mmBtu equivalent. December gas in New York was talked in the $3.90-4.00/mmBtu range versus NYH December one percent paper at a $3.31/mmBtu equivalent.
